A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Phased DMD. All 20 pages of each version, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy experiments, generated images and videos, quantitative diversity and motion evaluations, and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds video-quality metrics, a phase-count comparison and an expert-role visualization.

M1.justification: Progressive expert distillation, reverse-nested noise intervals, fake-model reinitialization and subinterval score-matching objectives remain unchanged. Four-phase distillation was already specified in v1; v2 evaluates that configuration and expands implementation documentation.

E1.justification: Both retain the four-value toy distribution, text-to-image evaluation with 21 prompts, and video evaluation with 220 text prompts and 220 image-prompt pairs. Added metrics and expert configurations do not introduce new datasets, tasks or domains.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the base models, vanilla few-step DMD and the SGTS-based baseline. V2 renames v1's 'DMD with SGTS' to 'DMD2'; matching descriptions and retained scores establish continuity. The four-phase variant is an ablation of the proposed method.

E3.justification: V2 adds FID/FVD against base-model outputs and five additional VBench metrics, plus four-phase and partial-expert evaluations. Table 1 changes the reported I2V teacher from Wan2.2-T2V-A14B to Wan2.2-I2V-A14B. The toy network description changes from four MLPs to a four-layer MLP; these reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a quantitative four-step/two-phase versus four-step/four-phase comparison testing complete SGTS removal with additional experts (Table 6). Figure 12 compares the low-SNR expert's two-step output with the complete four-step pipeline to examine expert roles. Existing noise-interval, fixed-noise and high-SNR-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify seeds 0–7 for image diversity and seed 42 for video evaluation, without repeated-training statistics, confidence intervals or significance tests. Parenthesized percentages in v2 Tables 4–5 are differences from base-model scores, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Phased DMD's reported T2V optical flow changes from 7.57 to 9.30 and dynamic degree from 74.55% to 82.27% under the stated four-step/two-phase setup, without explaining the revision. V2 adds FID/FVD, VBench and four-phase results; DMD2 leads all ten additional VBench metric columns. The image-diversity table remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 replaces v1 Eq. 8's approximation of scalar KL divergence by a teacher-minus-fake score expression with an explicit KL-gradient formulation in Eqs. 6–7. The subinterval derivations remain equivalent; the x-prediction objective already appeared in v1 Appendix A. Newly labeled estimator assumptions largely clarify existing requirements.

C1.justification: V2's abstract and introduction explicitly claim improved video visual fidelity alongside motion and image diversity, extending v1's emphasis on diversity and preservation of key capabilities. The central data-free framework, theoretical contribution and SOTA/largest-distillation claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 questions the additional VBench rankings using claimed human preferences and interprets proximity to teacher scores as distribution preservation. It attributes four-phase gains to both SGTS removal and additional parameters, acknowledges greater complexity, and recommends matching phases to teacher experts. Existing mechanism explanations and Qwen-Image diversity limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 64-GPU training, FSDP, checkpointing, context parallelism, Euler sampling, timestep schedules and shifts, resolution-sampling probabilities, noise clamps and phase-specific trainable components. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's optimizer and resolution settings. The promised code/model release becomes a stated availability link, whose contents were not externally checked.

R1.justification: V2 attributes SGTS to DMD2 as well as Self-Forcing, distinguishes its progression from step-halving progressive distillation, and softens TDM's formulation from 'incorrect' to 'suboptimal'. It adds citations including LCM, StyleGAN-V, DeepSeek-R1 and Qwen3 while removing several background references; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction and method exposition, organizes estimator requirements as explicit assumptions, and presents video experiments before image experiments. Appendix related work and toy details move into the main text, appendices are reorganized, and the standalone ethics and reproducibility statements are removed.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different visual template, expands setup and video-result tables, and adds Tables 4–6 and Figures 9 and 12. V1's separate appendix motion/camera figures become adjacent main-text figures with shortened captions, and image examples are rearranged. These are extensive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies previously missing implementation settings, corrects the KL derivation and adds useful fidelity and phase/expert evaluations, making the contribution easier to reproduce and assess. The gains are limited by unexplained headline T2V score replacements and an undocumented human-preference argument used to discount unfavorable VBench rankings.
